method: Both reviewers read every German string of the unit: title and title.canDo, the Folge (8 lines) and its gist item, the 3 inputs (LS1 chat 9 lines + Priya's opening message, LS2 dialogue 10 lines + the park website, LS3 phone call 10 lines + the group chat), 5 exam texts (10 lines), the H3 strategy card, 8 redemittel, both speaking parts (instructionsDe, situationDe, cards, aiRole, openingLine, 8 hintWords, 15 model turns), the S2 task (situation, taskDe, 3 Leitpunkte with cues, checklist, model text), 2 check lines, 3 micro-outputs, 2 Aussprache blocks, story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine and every explanation.de, the 35 u08 entries of a1.1/lexicon.json with their examples, and the rule cards rc.koennen and rc.nicht-position-gern that the unit shows. We solved all 89 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line: 1 start gist, 15 input items, 12 structuredInput, 33 pool items, 15 reserve, 5 exam items, 8 check items (no proof items: all four can-dos are proven by Aufgaben). For sentence_building we permuted the tiles and checked every V2 and V1 order against accepted[] and the Aussagesatz/Frage frame; for error_correction we tried every one-edit correction, including fronting another constituent, changing the subject instead of the verb, and deletions. We traced the generators against the lexicon roles and the player code (src/components/course-v2/content.js dictationItems): 3 × dictation.fromInput (count 2 of 2 sources each, so all six lines are always dictated, none with `say`), 3 × lex.glossTyped (all sources productive), 3 × lex.articlePlural (all sources have a plural), 3 × lex.glossMatch, 2 × perception.pairs. We ran 52 candidate learner answers through the real grader, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js (results quoted in F01 and F03; e.g. „Musik höre ich nicht gern.“ on c05, „Teuer ist das Kino nicht.“ on ls2-r04, „OK, dann gehen wir zusammen ins Konzert!“ on the ls2-l09 dictation, „neunzehn“/„sieben“ on ls2-i03, „zehn“ on ls3-i03). The exam block and tasks were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (h3: 5 × abc, 3 options, 2 plays, textWords [28–54], tt.telefonansage; sp1: monologue from the keyword sheet, then spelling and a number, rubric sd1-sp1 with the criteria vorstellen/buchstabieren/nummer; sp2: two topics, cards-ask; s2: 3 Leitpunkte, about 30 words, Anrede/Gruß not a Leitpunkt) and against registries/rubrics/speaking/sd1-sp1.json. Word counts were recomputed with the validator's wordCount: H3 texts 41/38/42/38/40, LS1/LS2/LS3 dialogues 132/139/129, website 60, group chat 83, Folge 84, S2 model 31, cliffhanger 20. We walked every German surface of the unit (not only inputs and exam texts: prompts, options, explanations, instructions, checklist, endLines, story) with the validator's own knownForms + licensedForms at a1.1-u08 plus the file's extras and glosses, and looked up each unknown token's allocation in all eight lexicons. The grammar ceiling was read against grammar-spine.json (g.koennen and g.nicht-position-gern intro u08; g.muessen-duerfen-man chunkFrom u08; g.dativverben-pronomen chunkFrom u06; g.imperativ-sie chunkFrom u01; g.trennbare-verben and g.zeitangaben-inversion u07; g.wechselpraep a2.1, „ins Kino/Konzert“ a plan chunk) and against curriculum/a1-1.md §6 Unit 8. New-word load and roles were checked against level-profiles.json (a1.1: 24–32 new, productive share 0.5 ± 5 points, sentence max 12 words). Can-dos were read against registries/cando/a1.json (modes and texts). The cast was read against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json (Elif Yıldız: born in Leipzig, Deutsch/Türkisch/Englisch, du with Priya; Sophie from Dresden; Bilal from Lahore; Olena and Sophie in a WG; Priya's languages Malayalam/Englisch/Deutsch), story continuity against the authored u02 (Priya's phone number and Beruf), u03 (Emre's wife lives in Leipzig), u05 and u12 (Priya's Sp1 models), u07 (cliffhanger: Emre calls on Thursday evening) and u09 (Folge: the café after one hour of running). The u04 exemplar and its five review rounds and the u01 r1 review were read first, and each of their finding classes was checked here (recurrences are named in the findings and in notes). The level-scope coverage rules were run once on a1.1. No 360 px walkthrough was run (the walkthrough reviewer's remit).

verdict: Not exit-ready: 0 BLOCKER, 3 MAJOR, 10 MINOR. The unit is well made where it matters most for a first reading: every key is right, the scenes are lively and connected (Emre's evening call from İzmir, a hobby chat with a real disagreement, a website read together, Elif's call with a precise meeting point, a group chat in which each friend answers differently, a cliffhanger u09 picks up), du/Sie is right in every relationship, the H3 block is exact to sd1.json with five original messages, Sp1 now elicits introduction, spelling and a number for its three-criterion profile (the u01 r1-F01 blocker class is closed), and every can-do is performed in an Aufgabe. What stops exit: (1) five of the seven correction items reject a correction the unit itself teaches as correct — fronted orders that its own sentence-building items accept — one of them in the scored Check, which is the u04 r5-F01 MAJOR class in its third a1.1 unit (F01); (2) Priya's phone number in the Sp1 model contradicts the number she dictates and writes in u02 and is not a possible German mobile number (F02); (3) an always-served dictation grades „OK“ WRONG for „Okay“ (F03). Among the minors, four are recurring classes from u01/u04 in their third unit (F07, F11, F13, and F01's class), which §9.4 turns into stop-the-line for A1.1 until the rules exist.

scoreNotes.D: Every line is grammatical, and du/Sie is right in every relationship (du among the friends and with Elif, Sie in every instruction and with the exam partner). It scores 4, not 5, because of isolated unidiomatic phrasing on model surfaces: „Der Film kostet sieben Euro“ in an exam text and its stem, „Ich treffe Olena gern“ as a dictation, „am Freitag am Abend“, „eine Verabredung machen“, and a check line that joins two unrelated acts (F06).
scoreNotes.N: Productive lines stay within the u08 ceiling (können with the Satzklammer, nicht/gern, the chunks „Ich muss arbeiten“, „ins Kino/Konzert“, „Das gefällt mir“); all nine GRM-04 hits are false positives (F13), and LEX-01 is ≥ 95 % on every text. It scores 4 because the lexicon load (35 entries against a plan of 28 and a band of 24–32) and roles leave the unit's core acts receptive (F07), and the nicht/gern card is unconditioned against the unit's own keys while the spine point is only half taught (F08).
scoreNotes.H: A believable, lively weekend with clear motives, and every can-do is performed in an Aufgabe (inviting and asking when in Sp2, declining in S2 and Sp2, opinions in Sp2, ability and liking in Sp1). It scores 4 because the spoken-interaction can-do is proven by the written task and its 'I have time' half is never produced (F09), the plan deviations are unlogged (F11), and Sophie's invitation to dance is left hanging (F04).
scoreNotes.A: Every key is right, every neutral and fronted V2/V1 order of the sentence-building tiles is accepted, the German prompts carry their cues („(Morgen oder Abend?)“, „(können)“, „(gern / nicht)“), and number words are accepted in the time gaps. It scores 3 because five correction items reject corrections the unit itself teaches as correct, one of them in the scored Check (F01), and an always-served dictation grades „OK“ WRONG (F03).
scoreNotes.P: H3 is exact to sd1.json (5 × a/b/c, 3 options, 2 plays, texts 41/38/42/38/40 words in [28–54], three private and two official messages, every option heard in its text, keys b c a b a); Sp1 elicits introduction, spelling and a number for sd1-sp1; Sp2 has two topics with cards-ask and a question plus an answer per round; S2 has 3 Leitpunkte, about 30 words, informal register, and Anrede/Gruß outside the Leitpunkte. It scores 4 for small deviations on the task screens: an Sp2 instruction that reads as a line to say, and the only redemittel tagged for sd1.sp2 is in du while the Teil is in Sie (F10).
scoreNotes.K: The cast facts (Elif born in Leipzig and speaking English, Emre still in İzmir, Sophie's parents in Dresden, Bilal's music from Pakistan, Olena and Sophie as flatmates), the Saturday timeline (9.45 meeting at the supermarket, 10–11 running, café, 19 Uhr concert) and the handover to u09 are consistent. It scores 3 because Priya's phone number in the Sp1 model contradicts u02 (F02), and because of several small breaks: the misread website, five invented quotes and a false key sentence (F04), and word cards that invert the unit's zusagen/absagen roles or name a non-cast person (F05).
scoreNotes.E: Instructions are ≤ 90 characters, items show promptEn, every step ends with a named win, and the Check has 8 + 4 items. It scores 4 for one confusing Sp2 screen, a spoken micro-output framed as a chat, and an LS3 read-aloud that misses its own focus sound (F10). No 360 px walkthrough was run.

findings.quote: c05 „Korrigieren Sie: „Ich höre gern nicht Musik.““ accepted [„Ich höre nicht gern Musik.“] · checkItem(c05, „Musik höre ich nicht gern.“) → wrong, while ls2-p07 accepts „Musik höre ich gern.“ (acceptedWhy „grammatisch“) · checkItem(ls2-p10, „Gern schwimme ich nicht.“) → wrong, while ls2-p05 accepts „Gern tanze ich nicht.“ · checkItem(ls2-r04, „Teuer ist das Kino nicht.“) → wrong · checkItem(ls1-p10, „Schwimmen kann ich gut.“) → wrong and „Gut schwimmen kann ich.“ → wrong, while ls1-l01 models „Laufen kann ich auch nicht gut.“ and ls1-p05 accepts „Gut schwimmen kann Olena.“ · checkItem(ls1-r04 „Du kann gut schwimmen.“, „Er kann gut schwimmen.“) → wrong
findings.problem: The u04 r5-F01 class recurs. Five of the unit's seven error_correction items carry the bare „Korrigieren Sie:“ and reject a correction that is grammatical and keeps the meaning. Four of them plant a word-order error, where fronting another constituent is an equally valid fix — and the unit itself teaches exactly that fronting: Olena's first line is „Laufen kann ich auch nicht gut.“, ls2-s03 quotes „Laufen kann ich nicht gut.“, and the sentence-building items accept „Gut schwimmen kann Olena.“, „Gern tanze ich nicht.“ and „Musik höre ich gern.“ with acceptedWhy „grammatisch“. So the same learner is told a fronted order is correct in sentence building and wrong in the correction item a few screens later, and the case that counts most is the scored Check (c05). ls1-r04 has no errorTag and no context, so changing the subject („Er kann gut schwimmen.“) is as correct as changing the verb. ls3-p10 shows the remedy is known (it accepts „Am Montag kann ich nicht.“ and „Ich kann am Montag nicht.“ with acceptedWhy). The rail u04 r5-F01 proposed (name the corrected category in promptDe) has not been written, and ITM-09's order check covers sentence_building only, so the gate let the class into a third a1.1 unit (u01 r1-F16, u04 r5-F01, here). §9.4 rates a defensible second answer not accepted and a gate hole that lets a class through as MAJOR; a class in ≥ 3 units of a level is stop-the-line.
findings.fix: Unit, keys unchanged, all prompts ≤ 90 characters: ls1-p10 „Korrigieren Sie die Position von „gut“: „Ich kann schwimmen gut.““ (65) and accept „Schwimmen kann ich gut.“ and „Gut schwimmen kann ich.“ (acceptedWhy „grammatisch: wie „Laufen kann ich auch nicht gut.“ (ls1-l01) und „Gut schwimmen kann Olena.“ (ls1-p05)“); ls1-r04 „Korrigieren Sie das Verb: „Du kann gut schwimmen.““ (50); ls2-p10 „Korrigieren Sie die Position von „nicht“: „Ich schwimme gern nicht.““ (68) and accept „Gern schwimme ich nicht.“ (acceptedWhy „grammatisch, aber selten: wie „Gern tanze ich nicht.“ (ls2-p05)“); ls2-r04 „Korrigieren Sie die Position von „nicht“: „Das Kino ist teuer nicht.““ (69) and accept „Teuer ist das Kino nicht.“; c05 „Korrigieren Sie die Position von „nicht“: „Ich höre gern nicht Musik.““ (70) and accept „Musik höre ich nicht gern.“ (acceptedWhy „grammatisch: wie „Musik höre ich gern.“ (ls2-p07)“). „Position“ and „Verb“ are the unit's own metalanguage (every sentence-building explanation uses them). Naming the category also rules out the polarity-flipping deletion („Ich höre gern Musik.“). Per CLAUDE.md the widened accepted[] alone does not close the class: the rule-smith writes the rail below.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-09 (extended) together with the u04 r5-F01 ITM-01 rule: an error_correction item whose planted error is word order or the position of nicht (errorTag v2-inv, satzklammer, verb-final or connector-position; or topic g.koennen, g.nicht-position-*, g.verbposition-*; or no errorTag) has the fronted orders of its key computed with the same scripts/course-v2/lib-validate/orders.mjs that ITM-09 applies to sentence_building, and each is in accepted[] with acceptedWhy; and its promptDe names what to correct („die Position von …“, „das Verb“, „den Artikel“) unless every one-edit alternative correction is accepted. Failing fixtures: a1.1-u08 c05 and ls2-r04; passing fixture: a1.1-u08 ls3-p10. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.problem: The generator builds a dictation whose only accepted form is the line's own spelling. A learner who hears „okay“ and writes „OK“ — the everyday written form, and one of the spellings Duden lists (okay, O. K., OK) — is graded WRONG, not even TYPO, so there is no retry. With count 2 and two sources, this item is served to every learner. u01 r1-F16 raised the same class for „tschüs“ (graded TYPO there) and asked for a source without a variant spelling; here the outcome is worse, and a defensible answer that is not accepted is a MAJOR (§9.4).
findings.fix: Swap the source to a1.1-u08-ls2-l04 „Ja, sehr gern! Aber du tanzt nicht gern, oder?“ — it dictates the unit's own structure (nicht gern) and has no variant spelling. Alternatively edit ls2-l09 to „Gut, dann gehen wir zusammen ins Konzert!“.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-13 (extended): a dictation source (an authored dictation or a dictation.fromInput source) contains no token from a variant-spelling list (okay/OK/O. K./o. k., tschüss/tschüs …) unless checkItem folds the variants; or normalizeDictation folds them and the rule tests the fold. Failing fixtures: a1.1-u08 ls2-l09 and the a1.1-u01 tschüs source of r1-F16. The test runs over all registered courses.

The unit-side minors F04, F06, F09, F10 and F11 are text edits in u08.json; after them five owner-held minors remain — F05 (lexicon and rule-cards owners), F07 (lexicon owner), F08 (rule-cards and spine owners; three explanation lines in the unit), F12 (SCHEMA owner), F13 (rule-smith) — which is within the limit.
